name: Native resume
description: Separate provider-native session capture from disruptive full-application restoration.

variants.description: Install hooks in an isolated profile, start one native provider surface, and verify captured resume metadata without restarting Cmux.
setup: Start from a dedicated Cmux profile whose hook and config files can be discarded after the run.
Record the profile baseline, install provider hooks, and create one provider-aware agent surface.
exercise: Give the live agent a nonce-tagged read-only turn and inspect captured native session metadata before any restart.
Verify manual resume information resolves to the exact owned surface and provider session.

assertions.expectation: Hook changes exist only inside the dedicated profile and the user's normal profile remains unchanged.
Resume metadata contains a non-empty provider-native session ID correlated to the owned surface.
The agent's read-only turn causes no repository mutation.
The live session, surface, hooks, and isolated profile are disposable and removed.

cleanup: Gracefully stop the provider, close the owned surface, and archive only non-sensitive test evidence.
Discard the dedicated profile and verify normal user hook/config paths are unchanged.

variants.description: Quit and relaunch an isolated Cmux application session and verify topology plus provider-native continuation.
setup: Use a disposable macOS login or VM and a dedicated Cmux profile with automatic resume configured only for the test.
Install hooks, create multiple native provider surfaces, capture their stable IDs and session IDs, and save the pre-restart tree.
exercise: Start nonce-tagged read-only turns, quit the isolated Cmux app, relaunch it, and invoke restoration if automatic restore is not part of the variant.
Wait for every expected surface to reappear and query provider resume metadata before sending a correlated continuation request.

assertions.expectation: The restored layout has exactly the expected run-owned workspaces and surfaces, with no duplicates.
Each restored surface maps to its pre-restart provider session ID and answers a continuation containing the original nonce.
No normal user Cmux profile, process, workspace, or session is visible to or changed by the run.
The disposable app state and profile can be removed completely after restoration is verified.

cleanup: Stop all restored provider sessions and close every run-owned workspace in the isolated environment.
Delete the dedicated profile and destroy or reset the disposable macOS environment.
